summary: The government's UAP infrastructure solidified this week with the establishment of a new interagency governance board tasked with coordinating investigations and declassification efforts across federal agencies. Complementing this bureaucratic shift, a science advisory council formed to inject fresh analytical approaches into the Pentagon's ongoing UAP work, with organizers emphasizing the need for "a completely different mindset" to make progress on the mystery. The third batch of Pentagon files under the PURSUE release program dropped, including assessments suggesting China and Russia may have recovered UAP objects, while separate documents showed the Department of War withholding core evaluation details on national security grounds. A public forum is now scheduled to let citizens hear directly from lawmakers and whistleblowers on disclosure matters, though debate continues over how much skepticism should balance advocacy on UAP panels. Separately, the Fiscal Year 2024 consolidated annual report on UAPs was added to government archives, and Congress set a June 30 briefing deadline for the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act to deliver updated UAP assessments.
